newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-McRetail H1 shr up, but motor weak.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-McRetail H1 shr up, but motor weak.

text.p: Analysts said on Friday McCarthy Retail Ltd would post an improvement in profits in the six months to December 1996, despite lower earnings from its motor division.
They said the retail division had managed a fairly strong performance and that the group's bottomline would be helped by a lower tax bill.
"I anticipate lower motor earnings in the first half of the year and some improvement in the second half of the year," Eric Levine, an analyst at Investec Securities told Reuters.
McCarthy last October said trading conditions in the first quarter of its 1996/97 financial year had been highly competitive due to disappointing growth in private consumption expenditure.
It said the reduction in prices of entry level cars had continued and resulted in further "write downs" of used vehicle stock.
Levine said McCarthy would do well if its motor earnings for the full 1996/97 year were able to equal those achieved last year.
Other analysts said group profits would, however, in the first half be boosted by a much lower tax charge after a heavy tax burden in the comparable period the year before.
"Their pre-tax earnings will be flat and will be helped by a lower tax rate," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast undiluted earnings per share rising to between 84.0 and 87.2 cents with consensus at 85.1 cents -- an improvement of just over 11 percent. They expected a dividend of 17.2 cents compared with 16.0.
McCarthy was expected to perform better in the second half of the year, they said.
